NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 879 6966 1697 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 879 6966 1697, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 10, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:21 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan & Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Administrative Aide Levi Sinkler

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-B, D-F AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF DECEMBER 2020 & JANUARY 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 64160 THROUGH 64199 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $405,675.69 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 080121 THROUGH
  080221 IN THE AMOUNT OF $75,607.46 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $481,283.15 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JUNE 28, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JULY 19, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
AUGUST 10, 2021
 F.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF AUGUST 2, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ abstained from item 5C, CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF
JULY 27, 2021.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JULY 27, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSTAIN:  Schmitz
  ABSENT:  None

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  CITY HALL COPY MACHINE LEASE

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted for the public that by entering into the proposed lease
with Canon, Canon will buy out the City’s last lease payment with the former copier.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead explained that a copier of this scale would cost
over $100,000 to purchase, with additional costs for servicing and maintaining the machine, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead noted that all hard drives on the old copier will be
wiped clean of all information before returning, in response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE STAFF TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH CANON
  SOLUTIONS AMERICA & CANON FINANCIAL SERVICES FOR THE LEASE
  OF THE CANON COPIER AND ENTER INTO A MAINTENANCE
  AGREEMENT FOR THE TERM OF THE LEASE SUBJECT TO FINAL
  REVIEW BY THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  JOINT PENINSULA LETTER OPPOSING AB 215

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), noting that AB
215 would require a jurisdiction with low regional housing needs progress to have a mid-cycle
consultation with the California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
AUGUST 10, 2021
 Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE LETTER OPPOSING AB 215.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT UPDATE

Administrative Aide Sinkler provided a presentation of the City’s public engagement over the
last year.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ thanked Administrative Aide Sinkler and staff for their
successful community engagement through all of the City’s platforms over the past year.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF echoed COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ’s sentiments regarding
staff’s effective communication with the community.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

This item was received and filed by the Council.

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order
is still in effect requiring masks for all indoor public settings, regardless of vaccination status.
There has been an increase both in the number of COVID cases and hospitalizations, with
unvaccinated people making up the majority of hospitalizations. Vaccination rates in Rolling
Hills Estates are currently as follows: ages 12 and older with at least 1 dose = 84%, ages
12-17 = 94%, and ages 65 and older = 97%.

City events are continuing as planned, including the Hills Are Alive race that took place last
Saturday. There will be another Movie in the Park event later this month, the City Celebration
in September, the Tracy Austin Tournament tentatively this fall, and the Holiday Parade in
December.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  JOINT PENINSULA LETTER TO L.A. COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS AND
  DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH

City Manager Grammer provided a brief report regarding a draft joint letter from the four
Peninsula Mayors to the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors and the Department of
Public Health calling for the indoor masking mandate to be rescinded for individuals who are
fully vaccinated.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF spoke against signing the proposed letter.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ spoke in favor of signing the proposed letter.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
AUGUST 10, 2021
 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA spoke against signing the proposed letter.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN spoke in favor of signing the proposed letter.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN spoke against signing the proposed letter.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the Los Angeles Division of the League of California
Cities Officer Installation last week.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also attended the Palos Verdes Chamber of Commerce
Legislative Committee meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported on the successful National Night Out event last week.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager (Annual Evaluation)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)
  Initiation of litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:18 P.M. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting to Tuesday,
August 24, 2021 at 7:00 P.M. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Steve Zuckerman
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
AUGUST 10, 2021
